criteria.criterion: Every user-facing error string the CLI prints is defined exactly once, in src/runstat/messages.py
criteria.evidence: src/runstat/cli.py:13 defines `_PREFIX = "runstat: "`, a duplicate of messages.PREFIX (messages.py:9). The prefix, which is prepended to every error line, exists in two places.

criteria.criterion: cli.py refers to those strings by name; no error literal or error prefix is written inline in cli.py
criteria.evidence: src/runstat/cli.py:13 `_PREFIX = "runstat: "` is an error prefix literal written inline in cli.py, in direct violation of this criterion.

criteria.criterion: A missing run directory exits 2, with the catalogue's text on stderr
criteria.evidence: cli.py:26 calls `_fail(f"{messages.BAD_RUN_DIR}: {args.run_dir}", 2)`; messages.BAD_RUN_DIR = "run directory not found". Verified: `uv run pytest -q tests/test_messages.py` passes 2/2, including test_missing_run_dir_exits_2_with_catalogue_text.

criteria.criterion: Changing an error's wording requires editing only src/runstat/messages.py
criteria.evidence: Changing the prefix wording requires editing both messages.py (PREFIX) and cli.py (_PREFIX). The code's own comment at cli.py:12-14 admits this: 'Declared here rather than taken from messages.PREFIX ... Keep in sync with messages.PREFIX by hand if the wording changes.'

criteria.criterion: stdout is completely empty on every failing path
criteria.evidence: _fail() (cli.py:16-18) only ever writes to sys.stderr; every failing branch in _cmd_signals and main returns via _fail before any stdout print. No print() call in cli.py targets stdout on a failing path.

findings: cli.py:9-14 hardcodes its own copy of the error prefix (_PREFIX = "runstat: ") instead of importing messages.PREFIX, reintroducing the exact drift the catalogue task exists to remove — and the accompanying comment acknowledges the two must be kept in sync by hand.
messages.py defines PREFIX but nothing in cli.py ever references it, so the catalogue's own prefix constant is dead code.
notes: The gate test (tests/test_messages.py::test_cli_declares_its_error_prefix) only asserts that the literal string "runstat: " appears somewhere in cli.py's source text, so it passes regardless of whether the prefix comes from messages.py or is redeclared locally. It does not distinguish `messages.PREFIX` usage from a hardcoded duplicate, so a green gate here does not establish that this criterion is met. The fix is for cli.py to use messages.PREFIX (e.g. `_fail` formatting with `messages.PREFIX` instead of a locally declared `_PREFIX`) and for messages.py to be the sole definition site.
